newsitem.title: FINLAND: NIINISTO HOPEFUL ON FINLAND CREDIT RATING UPGRADES.
newsitem.headline: NIINISTO HOPEFUL ON FINLAND CREDIT RATING UPGRADES.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto
said on Wednesday he saw hope for upgrading of Finland's credit
ratings by leading rating institutes and said upgrades may have
been delayed because of timetables.
"We seem to be partly victims of timetables, but the
positive country reports do give hopes (of upgrades) and also
there have been very little complaints," Niinisto told a
seminar.
A finance ministry official said earlier this week that a
scheduled early-autumn Standard & Poor's visit to Finland had
been postponed to an unspecified later date in 1996.
A team from Moody's was also likely to visit Finland this
autumn, the official said.
Niinisto repeated that Finnish 1991-1997 budget spending
cuts would total 10 percent of GDP, which he said was
unsurpassed in any other OECD country.
Finland currently has the following long term foreign
currency debt ratings:
Standard & Poor's AA-/outlook positive
outlook changed from stable August/95
Moody's Aa2
issued January/92
IBCA AA/outlook positive
issued March/96
